title: Cocaine Detox Timeline, Explained
metaDescription: Detox is often the initial step for those with severe addiction disorders. Learn the cocaine detox timeline and how to find detox near you.

blocks.text: If you or someone you love has struggled to detox from cocaine on their own, that’s probably because the cocaine detox timeline takes a long time and requires medical supervision to be done effectively. Thankfully, there is professional help available, and you can successfully manage your cocaine withdrawal under medical supervision.

Cocaine is an addictive stimulant that comes from the coca leaf in South America. Today cocaine is a schedule II drug because of the high risk of addiction. It is still used today for medical purposes, specifically as a pain management drug for surgery or local anesthesia.

Yes, cocaine withdrawal is real, and detox from cocaine should be done under medical supervision. Withdrawal from cocaine is more psychological than physical, so some people may not even realize that cocaine can cause significant withdrawal, just like alcohol addiction or addiction to benzodiazepines.
What are the Symptoms of Cocaine Withdrawal?

Cocaine withdrawal symptoms can vary in terms of their severity when you set about a detox from cocaine. Understanding the way in which the cocaine detox timeline works and how it can vary from one person to another is important.
What is the Cocaine Detox Timeline?
The cocaine detox timeline spans between 7 and 10 days.
Symptoms begin 90 minutes after the last dose. Cocaine remains in your system for about 6 hours after you have taken your last dose, which is why these symptoms happen so suddenly.

The symptoms of acute cocaine withdrawal typically go away after about one week, but the cravings can take place for much longer. Even after these Maine physical and psychological symptoms of cocaine withdrawal subside, it takes about two hundred days before you no longer have any cravings.

How long the cocaine detox timeline lasts for each individual is based on things like how long they have used cocaine, what amounts of cocaine have been used, whether there are any other drugs being used, and whether there are any co-occurring mental health problems or medical health problems.
